CMATS burden-augmented adaptive omnibus association test

Source: vignettes/method-cmats.Rmd
method-cmats.Rmd

Function: run_cmats()

Result column: cmats

Family: Adaptive MATS/SKAT-O style

Introduction

Multi-phenotype association test that adaptively blends a variance-component (Wald / SKAT-style) statistic with a directional burden statistic over a grid of mixing weights, in the spirit of the SKAT-O optimal unified test (Lee et al. 2012; Wu et al. 2011). The per-variant minimum p-value over the grid is calibrated against its analytic null distribution.

Mathematical Framework and Implementation

For each variant let z=(z1,…,zK)′z=(z_1,\dots,z_K)' be the vector of per-trait Z-scores, zk=β̂k/sekz_k=\hat\beta_k/\mathrm{se}_k, and let Σ\Sigma be the K×KK\times K trait correlation matrix with inverse Σ−1\Sigma^{-1}, a=Σ−1𝟏a=\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1} and s=𝟏′Σ−1𝟏=∑ij(Σ−1)ijs=\mathbf{1}'\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}=\sum_{ij}(\Sigma^{-1})_{ij}.

Two component statistics are formed. The variance-component (Wald) term is the Mahalanobis quadratic form

χ1=z′Σ−1z, \chi_1 = z'\Sigma^{-1}z,

which under the global null is χ2\chi^2 with KK degrees of freedom. The burden term aggregates a Σ−1\Sigma^{-1}-weighted sum of Z-scores,

χ2=(a′z)2s=(𝟏′Σ−1z)2𝟏′Σ−1𝟏, \chi_2 = \frac{(a'z)^2}{s} = \frac{(\mathbf{1}'\Sigma^{-1}z)^2}{\mathbf{1}'\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}},

which under the null is χ2\chi^2 with 11 degree of freedom.

For each ρ\rho on the grid {0,0.1,…,1}\{0,0.1,\dots,1\} (11 equally spaced points) the mixed statistic

Qρ=(1−ρ)χ1+ρχ2 Q_\rho = (1-\rho)\,\chi_1 + \rho\,\chi_2

is computed. Its null tail probability pρp_\rho is obtained exactly at the endpoints (χK2\chi^2_K for ρ=0\rho=0, χ12\chi^2_1 for ρ=1\rho=1) and otherwise as the tail of a weighted sum of independent χ12\chi^2_1 variables with eigenvalue spectrum (1−ρ)(1-\rho) with multiplicity K−1K-1 and a single eigenvalue 11, evaluated by the Liu moment-matching approximation. The test statistic is the minimum p-value

T=minρpρ. T = \min_\rho p_\rho.

Because the QρQ_\rho are dependent, the final p-value corrects the minimum-p statistic with the SKAT-O one-dimensional null integral

p=minρpρ+∫0tmaxPr⁡[χK−12>mini:ρi<1qi−x(t)1−ρi]dt, p = \min_\rho p_\rho + \int_0^{t_{\max}} \Pr\Big[\chi^2_{K-1} > \min_{i:\,\rho_i<1}\frac{q_i - x(t)}{1-\rho_i}\Big]\,dt,

where qiq_i is the quantile of the mixed null at level 1−min⁡ρpρ1-\min_\rho p_\rho for grid point ii, x(t)x(t) is the χ12\chi^2_1 quantile at tt, and tmaxt_{\max} is the upper limit set by the ρ=1\rho=1 quantile. The integral is evaluated numerically by composite Simpson’s rule, and the result is clamped to [0,1][0,1].

What This Method Advances

CMATS adapts the SKAT-O idea to multi-trait summary statistics by blending a full Wald component with a burden component.

Assumptions

Z-scores are approximately multivariate normal with mean zero and covariance Σ\Sigma under the global null of no association with any trait. Σ\Sigma is the (full-rank, invertible) trait correlation matrix shared across variants and is treated as known. Variants are tested one at a time; the omnibus combines information across the KK traits, not across variants.

When This Method Is a Good Fit

Good when either a full multivariate signal or a common burden-like direction could be present.

The implementation treats variants independently and relies on the trait-correlation estimate derived from the available summary statistics unless an individual method estimates a pairwise null moment internally.

Minimal Usage 

library(pleioverse)
set.seed(1)
pleio <- run_pleiosim(
  n_phenotype = 3, n_participant = 500,
  n_variant_pleiotropic = 3,
  n_variant_nonpleiotropic = c(3, 3, 3),
  n_variant_null = 30,
  heritability = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
)
pleio <- run_cmats(pleio)
head(pleio@results$cmats)

Implementation Files

  • R wrapper: R/run_cmats.R
  • C++ kernel or dispatcher: src/mats.cpp
  • Shared MPAT inputs, where applicable: R/pleiotest.R and src/test_engine.cpp

References

Wu MC, Lee S, Cai T, Li Y, Boehnke M, Lin X (2011). Rare-variant association testing for sequencing data with the sequence kernel association test (SKAT). Am J Hum Genet 89(1):82-93. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajhg.2011.05.029

Lee S, Wu MC, Lin X (2012). Optimal tests for rare variant effects in sequencing association studies. Biostatistics 13(4):762-775. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1093/biostatistics/kxs014

Liu H, Tang Y, Zhang HH (2009). A new chi-square approximation to the distribution of non-negative definite quadratic forms in non-central normal variables. Comput Stat Data Anal 53(4):853-856. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csda.2008.11.025
